title: Fixed Folded Arrow Fluke and Curved Eyed Shank Anchor
description: One newly authored complete fixed plough-anchor-inspired exterior. One full thick arrow-shaped fluke has a narrow blunt nose, two broad uninterrupted wings, a real rear chevron indentation, one raised longitudinal top fold and an integral finite flat keel sole beneath its otherwise rising lower wing faces. A separate complete curved solid shank roots into the rear centre, rises and returns forward over the open space above the fluke, ending in one whole open attachment eye with a genuine transverse bore. All three complete closed meshes are newly authored together; the fluke is not two detached palms or a cropped agricultural share, and the shank is not an extracted handle or old anchor arm. No timber stock, round cupped mushroom crown, central straight mast, separate handles, landside runner, chains or plinth. Unlike the stocked twin-fluke anchor, there is no opposed pair of upturned arms and perpendicular stock; unlike the circular cupped anchor, the broad folded arrow and low forward-returning shank form a lengthwise asymmetrical profile. Unlike the agricultural plough, there is no curling longitudinal mouldboard, wood drawbeam or two rear handles. Three whole editable material meshes, two opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and whole horizontal bounds-centred origin on the integral keel. One independent static model zero scenes. Generic plough-anchor vocabulary only, original artistic profile, proportions and blunt surfaces, not a branded product, replica of a museum object or maritime standard. Selected finite static roots, ground sole, bore and under-shank gaps do not establish seabed embedment, holding force, pull direction, mooring, articulation, vessel compatibility, stability, strength, casting, manufacture, salvage, anchoring procedure or maritime/public safety capability. No fluid, rigging, animation or interaction.
